title: 9.2 Small Group · Group 2
contentObjective: I can use a table and a graph to determine and analyze the relationship between two variable quantities, explain what each part stands for, and build one for a situation I have not seen before.
languageObjective: I can justify my answer to a skeptic and connect it to a second strategy or representation.

noticeAndWonder.context: A ticket to a college football game costs $45. Next to the ticket is a table: 1 ticket, $45. 2 tickets, $90. 3 tickets, $135. Beside the table is a graph with points climbing up and to the right.
noticeStarters: I notice the graph's points go ___ .
I notice the table and graph show ___ .
wonderStarters: I wonder what the fourth ticket point ___ .
I wonder why the graph and table ___ .
I wonder what happens to the graph ___ .
noticeAndWonder.imageAlt: A cable car suspended on a wire, travelling above a lake and green hillside.

vocabulary.definition: A picture on a coordinate plane that shows how two quantities are related.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un dibujo en un plano de coordenadas que muestra cómo se relacionan dos cantidades.
vocabulary.example: The football ticket graph shows cost rising as tickets increase.
vocabulary.visual: Points (1, 45), (2, 90), (3, 135) climbing left to right — cost by tickets.
vocabulary.cloze: A picture on the coordinate plane showing how two quantities relate is a ___.

examples.text: Plotted points where each one is a (tickets, cost) pair
examples.why: Every point carries both quantities at once.
A picture with no quantities on it shows no relationship.

vocabulary.definition: A list of matched pairs of values that shows a relationship using numbers.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una lista de pares de valores que muestra una relación usando números.
vocabulary.example: The ticket table pairs 3 tickets with $135.
vocabulary.visual: months 1, 2, 4 beside cost 24.95, 49.90, 99.80 — one row per pair.
vocabulary.cloze: A list of matched pairs that shows a relationship in numbers is a ___ ___ ___.

examples.text: Hours in one column, kilometers in the other
examples.why: Each row pairs the two quantities at the same moment.

examples.text: A column of costs with nothing to pair them to
examples.why: One quantity alone shows no relationship.

vocabulary.definition: Two numbers written as (x, y) that name one point on a graph. The independent variable comes first.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos números escritos como (x, y) que nombran un punto en la gráfica. La variable independiente va primero.
vocabulary.visual: (3, 135): 3 tickets cost $135 — the independent quantity comes first.
vocabulary.cloze: Two numbers written (x, y) that name one point are an ___ ___.

examples.why: Reversed, it plots a different point.

vocabulary.definition: One of the two number lines that frame a graph. Each axis is labeled with a quantity from the problem.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una de las dos rectas numéricas que enmarcan una gráfica. Cada eje se rotula con una cantidad del problema.
vocabulary.example: One axis shows the number of tickets; the other shows the total cost.
vocabulary.visual: Horizontal axis: months. Vertical axis: total cost.
vocabulary.cloze: Each number line framing a graph, labeled with a quantity, is an ___.

examples.text: The horizontal line labeled “number of tickets”
examples.why: It is one of the two lines, and it names a quantity.

examples.text: The line connecting the plotted points

vocabulary.definition: The numbers in an ordered pair that tell how far to move along each axis to reach a point.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Los números de un par ordenado que indican cuánto avanzar por cada eje para llegar a un punto.

vocabulary.visual: In (4, 105), 4 says how far across and 105 how far up.

examples.why: They locate the point on each axis.
A label names an axis; it is not a number.

turnAndTalk.question: Football tickets cost $45 each: 1 ticket is $45, 2 tickets are $90, 3 tickets are $135. When you write the ordered pair for 3 tickets, which number goes first — 3 or 135 — and why?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The number of tickets is the independent variable, and the independent variable always comes first in an ordered pair, so the point is (3, 135), not (135, 3).

stems.en: The ordered pair is (___, ___) because ___ comes first.
stems.es: El par ordenado es (___, ___) porque ___ va primero.

stems.en: If I wrote (135, 3) instead, that would mean ___.
stems.es: Si escribiera (135, 3) en cambio, eso significaría ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: The Sandia Peak tram travels 1,200 feet each minute. Justify why the point for 5 minutes is (5, 6000) and not (6000, 5), using the same rule you used for the tickets.
extendStems: Minutes is independent because ___, so it goes ___ in the pair.
(6000, 5) would be wrong because it would mean ___.

turnAndTalk.question: You sorted cards like '(4, 190) is a point on the graph' into matches and non-matches for cost = 45 × tickets. How did you check each one?
turnAndTalk.kernel: A point (tickets, cost) matches the relationship only if cost equals 45 times the number of tickets.

stems.en: I checked (___, ___) by multiplying ___ × 45 and comparing it to ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: Card '(1, 55) is a point on the graph' was also NOT a match. What single mistake would produce 55 instead of the correct value — and how is that different from the mistake in (4, 190)?
extendStems: 55 could come from ___ instead of multiplying, while 190 looks like a different kind of error: ___.
Both are wrong, but for different reasons: ___ versus ___.

turnAndTalk.question: Nakai's account starts with $750 and earns the same $26.25 every year. Why does the interest graph rise in a straight line instead of curving upward more steeply each year?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Simple interest is calculated only on the original $750 principal, so the SAME amount, $26.25, is added every year — a constant increase makes a straight line, not a curve.

stems.en: The graph is straight because every year adds exactly $___.
stems.es: La gráfica es recta porque cada año se suman exactamente $___.

stems.en: If the interest grew faster each year, that would mean ___ instead of simple interest.
stems.es: Si el interés creciera más rápido cada año, eso significaría ___ en lugar de interés simple.

turnAndTalk.extend: A point on Nakai's graph is (4, x). Find x, and explain how you know your answer is NOT the account's total balance after 4 years.
extendStems: x = ___ because 4 years of $26.25 each is 4 × ___.
That is not the total balance because the balance would also include the ___ of $750.

turnAndTalk.question: Look back at a problem where you found coordinates for a point. What was your process from the rate to the final ordered pair?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Every ordered pair on a rate graph comes from multiplying the rate by the independent variable's value, then writing (independent, dependent).

stems.en: I started with the rate, $___ per ___, then multiplied by ___ to get the total.
stems.es: Empecé con la tasa, $___ por ___, luego multipliqué por ___ para obtener el total.

stems.en: I know my ordered pair is correct because ___.
stems.es: Sé que mi par ordenado es correcto porque ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: A classmate wrote the point for 4 tickets as (4, 49) instead of (4, 180). What operation mistake would produce 49, and how would you help them catch it?
extendStems: 49 looks like they ___ instead of multiplying 4 × 45.
I'd tell them to check by ___ before trusting the answer.

launch.narrative: This is your challenge small group for Lesson 9.2. You can already get the answer — so in here the answer is the starting point. We ask when the method holds, when it breaks, and how you would convince someone who disagrees.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — Two pictures of the same relationship
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. So we go up a level, not up a number: find what is always true, show it a second way, and be ready to defend it with a reason instead of an answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Each row of the table becomes one ordered pair — (independent variable, dependent variable) — plotted as one point on the graph — and you can say why it is true, and where it would stop being true.

iDo.title: Watch me build the ticket graph
lines: Each ticket costs $45, so the total cost is 45 times the number of tickets: 1 ticket is $45, 2 tickets are $90, 3 tickets are $135.
The number of tickets is the independent variable, so it goes first in each ordered pair: (1, 45), (2, 90), (3, 135).
I label one axis 'Number of tickets' and the other 'Total cost ($)', then plot each pair as a point.
The points rise to the right: as the number of tickets increases, the total cost increases.
linesEs: Cada boleto cuesta $45, así que el costo total es 45 por el número de boletos: 1 boleto son $45, 2 boletos son $90, 3 boletos son $135.
El número de boletos es la variable independiente, así que va primero en cada par ordenado: (1, 45), (2, 90), (3, 135).
Rotulo un eje como «Número de boletos» y el otro como «Costo total ($)», y luego marco cada par como un punto.
Los puntos suben hacia la derecha: conforme aumenta el número de boletos, aumenta el costo total.
iDo.titleEs: Mírame armar la gráfica de los boletos

weDo.title: Try it together — then prove it
lines: The tram travels 1,200 feet every minute. Which quantity is independent — time or distance?
Time is independent, so our pairs look like (minutes, feet): (1, 1200), (2, 2400), (5, 6000).
The ascent takes 15 minutes, so the last point is (15, 18000) — because 15 times 1,200 is 18,000 feet.
Each point means: after THIS many minutes, the tram has traveled THIS many feet.
Now prove it: say why that move had to work at all — not just that it did.
Sentence frame — convince a skeptic: "My method works because ___ . It would stop working if ___ ."
linesEs: El teleférico recorre 1,200 pies cada minuto. ¿Qué cantidad es independiente — el tiempo o la distancia?
El tiempo es independiente, así que nuestros pares se ven como (minutos, pies): (1, 1200), (2, 2400), (5, 6000).
El ascenso toma 15 minutos, así que el último punto es (15, 18000) — porque 15 por 1,200 son 18,000 pies.
Cada punto significa: después de estos minutos, el teleférico ha recorrido estos pies.
Ahora demuéstralo: di por qué ese paso tenía que funcionar — no solo que funcionó.
Marco de oración — convence a alguien que duda: «Mi método funciona porque ___ . Dejaría de funcionar si ___ .»

youDo.title: Now you try — and defend it
lines: Try the problems below on your own. Getting the answer is half the work — be ready to say why your method works, and where it would stop working.
Then pick one problem and show it a second way. If two different methods agree, that agreement is your proof.
linesEs: Intenta los problemas de abajo por tu cuenta. Obtener la respuesta es la mitad del trabajo — prepárate para decir por qué funciona tu método y dónde dejaría de funcionar.
Luego elige un problema y muéstralo de una segunda manera. Si dos métodos distintos coinciden, esa coincidencia es tu prueba.

conceptIntro.headingEs: Ve más allá — Dos imágenes de la misma relación
conceptIntro.introEs: Esto ya lo sabes hacer. Así que subimos de nivel, no de número: halla lo que siempre es cierto, muéstralo de una segunda manera y prepárate para defenderlo con una razón en lugar de una respuesta.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: Cada fila de la tabla se vuelve un par ordenado — (variable independiente, variable dependiente) — marcado como un punto en la gráfica — y puedes decir por qué es cierto y dónde dejaría de serlo.

explore.label: Tickets cost $45 each, so the total cost is 45 times the number of tickets. Sort each statement: does it MATCH the ticket relationship, or NOT?

cards.text: (2, 90) is a point on the graph
(3, 135) is a point on the graph

explore.instructions: Go deeper: Sort all eight cards. For each ordered pair, multiply the first number by 45 and check whether it equals the second number. As you work, ask yourself WHY it works.

connect.scenario: Nakai opened a savings account with an initial deposit, or principal, of $750. The account earns 3.5% simple interest each year — interest is the amount earned for the use of the principal. A graph shows the interest Nakai has earned over a period of years, with points rising steadily.
connect.promptQuestion: What observations can you make about the data using the graph?
connect.prompt: ___ is the independent variable, while ___ is the dependent variable. As the years go by, the interest earned ___, because each year adds $___ to the total.

check.stem: On Nakai's graph, which variable is plotted on the independent axis (x-axis)?
check.explanation: Years is the independent variable because interest earned changes as a result of how many years have passed, not the other way around. Interest earned is dependent; the principal ($750) is a fixed starting value, not a changing quantity being graphed; account balance combines principal and interest, which isn't what this graph plots.

check.stem: Why does the graph rise by the same amount every year instead of curving upward more steeply over time?
choices: Nakai earns simple interest — the same $26.25 each year, calculated only on the original $750 principal
Nakai earns compound interest, which grows faster each year
The interest rate increases by 3.5% every year
Nakai deposits an extra $26.25 into the account every year
check.explanation: Simple interest is calculated only on the original principal each year, so the account gains a constant $26.25 annually, producing a straight (linear) rise. Compound interest would make the graph curve upward faster, a rising rate would change the yearly amount, and extra deposits would not be interest at all.

check.stem: A point on the graph is located at (4, x). Based on the interest rate, what value of x makes this point correct?
check.explanation: After 4 years Nakai has earned 4 × $26.25 = $105 in interest. $78.75 is only 3 years' worth of interest, $855 confuses interest earned with the total account balance (principal plus interest), and $131.25 is 5 years' worth.

connect.modelAnswer: The number of years is the independent variable and the interest earned is the dependent variable. The graph rises steadily because Nakai earns the same amount every year — 3.5% of $750 is $26.25. A point like (2, 52.50) means that after 2 years Nakai has earned $52.50 in interest, since 2 × 26.25 = 52.50.

exitTicket.stem: Explain your thinking — On the football ticket graph, what does the point (3, 135) represent?
exitTicket.explanation: The independent variable comes first in an ordered pair. Here that is the number of tickets, so 3 is the tickets. Then find the cost: 3 × $45 = $135. The point pairs 3 tickets with a total cost of $135.
hints: Which quantity comes first in an ordered pair — the independent or dependent variable?
The number of tickets is the independent variable here.
Check the arithmetic: what is 3 × 45?

onLevel.stem: The Sandia Peak tram travels 1,200 feet each minute and the ascent takes 15 minutes. How long is the whole ascent in feet?
choiceFeedback: That adds 1,200 + 15 instead of multiplying 1,200 × 15.
12,000 feet is the distance after 10 minutes, not the full 15.
16,800 feet is the distance after 14 minutes — one minute short of the top.
hints: How many minutes does the full ascent take?
Each of those 15 minutes covers 1,200 feet.
Multiply 1,200 by 15.
onLevel.stemEs: El tranvía de Sandia Peak recorre 1,200 pies por minuto y el ascenso toma 15 minutos. ¿Cuánto mide todo el ascenso en pies?
hintsEs: ¿Cuántos minutos toma todo el ascenso?
Cada uno de esos 15 minutos cubre 1,200 pies.
Multiplica 1,200 por 15.
choicesEs: 18,000 pies
1,215 pies
12,000 pies
16,800 pies

onLevel.stem: On the tram graph with minutes on the horizontal axis and feet on the vertical axis, which ordered pair lies on the graph?
onLevel.explanation: After 5 minutes the tram has traveled 5 × 1,200 = 6,000 feet, so the point is (5, 6000).
choiceFeedback: You reversed the coordinates — time (the independent variable) goes first.
1,200 feet is the distance for 1 minute, not 5.
5,000 rounds the rate to 1,000 feet per minute — the tram travels 1,200 feet each minute.
hints: Which axis is time on?
The second coordinate is the distance after 5 minutes.
Multiply 5 by 1,200.
onLevel.stemEs: En la gráfica del tranvía con los minutos en el eje horizontal y los pies en el eje vertical, ¿cuál par ordenado está en la gráfica?
onLevel.explanationEs: Después de 5 minutos el tranvía ha recorrido 5 × 1,200 = 6,000 pies, así que el punto es (5, 6000).
hintsEs: ¿En cuál eje va el tiempo?
La segunda coordenada es la distancia después de 5 minutos.
Multiplica 5 por 1,200.

onLevel.stem: Why is the line on the football ticket graph dashed instead of solid?
choices: You can only buy whole numbers of tickets, so the points between whole numbers do not make sense
Dashed lines always mean the cost is decreasing
The ticket price changes between points
onLevel.explanation: You cannot buy 2.5 tickets. So only the whole-number points represent real purchases. The dashes still show the trend between them. They just do not claim the in-between points are possible.
choiceFeedback: The graph is complete — the dashes are a deliberate choice about what the in-between values mean.
Dashes say nothing about direction; this cost is increasing.
The price stays $45 per ticket everywhere on the graph.
hints: Could you buy half a ticket?
Which points on the line represent real purchases?
Only whole numbers of tickets make sense here.
onLevel.stemEs: ¿Por qué la línea de la gráfica de boletos de fútbol americano es punteada en vez de continua?
onLevel.explanationEs: No puedes comprar 2.5 boletos. Así que solo los puntos con números enteros representan compras reales. Las líneas punteadas muestran la tendencia entre ellos. Simplemente no afirman que los puntos intermedios sean posibles.
hintsEs: ¿Podrías comprar medio boleto?
¿Cuáles puntos de la línea representan compras reales?
Aquí solo tienen sentido los números enteros de boletos.
choicesEs: Solo se pueden comprar números enteros de boletos, así que los puntos entre números enteros no tienen sentido
La gráfica está incompleta
Las líneas punteadas siempre significan que el costo está bajando
El precio del boleto cambia entre un punto y otro

onLevel.label: Tickets cost $45 each. Complete the table that feeds the graph.
onLevel.labelEs: Los boletos cuestan $45 cada uno. Completa la tabla que alimenta la gráfica.
hints: The independent variable (tickets) goes in column 1; the dependent (cost) responds in the last column.
Each completed row becomes one point on the graph: (tickets, cost).
hintsEs: La variable independiente (boletos) va en la columna 1; la dependiente (costo) responde en la última columna.
Cada fila completada se convierte en un punto de la gráfica: (boletos, costo).
onLevel.explanation: Each row multiplies by the $45 rate: (2, 90), (5, 225), (8, 360). Those three rows ARE three points of the graph — a table and a graph are two views of the same relationship, which is the central idea of this lesson.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada fila multiplica por la tarifa de $45: (2, 90), (5, 225), (8, 360). Esas tres filas son tres puntos de la gráfica: una tabla y una gráfica son dos vistas de la misma relación, la idea central de esta lección.

extending.instructions: Tickets cost $45 each. Plot the points for 1, 2, 3, and 4 tickets on the graph of tickets vs. total cost.
extending.instructionsEs: Los boletos cuestan $45 cada uno. Ubica los puntos para 1, 2, 3 y 4 boletos en la gráfica de boletos contra costo total.
extending.label: Plot the ticket-cost relationship: one point for each number of tickets.
extending.labelEs: Ubica la relación boletos-costo: un punto por cada cantidad de boletos.
hints: Each gridline on the vertical axis is worth $45 — one ticket's price.
After plotting, look at the shape: every extra ticket raises the cost by the same amount.
hintsEs: Cada línea de la cuadrícula en el eje vertical vale $45: el precio de un boleto.
Después de ubicar los puntos, observa la forma: cada boleto adicional sube el costo la misma cantidad.
extending.explanation: The four points (1, 45), (2, 90), (3, 135), (4, 180) line up on a straight path from the origin: each extra ticket adds exactly $45. That constant climb IS the rate of change, and seeing it in the lined-up points is what 'analyzing a graph' means in this lesson.
extending.explanationEs: Los cuatro puntos (1, 45), (2, 90), (3, 135), (4, 180) se alinean en una trayectoria recta desde el origen: cada boleto adicional suma exactamente $45. Esa subida constante ES la tasa de cambio, y verla en los puntos alineados es lo que significa 'analizar una gráfica' en esta lección.

extending.stem: The ticket table and ticket graph are two representations. Which statement about them is true?
choices: Both show the same relationship — the table with numerical values, the graph in a more visual way
The graph shows a different relationship than the table
Only the table can show that cost increases with tickets
Only the graph is a real mathematical representation
extending.explanation: Every row of the table is plotted as a point, so both show cost = 45 × tickets — the table numerically, the graph visually.
choiceFeedback: Each point on the graph comes straight from a row of the table — they show the SAME relationship.
The graph also shows the increase: the points rise to the right.
Tables are just as mathematical as graphs — they show the same pairs of values.
hints: Where do the graph's points come from?
Each table row becomes one point.
Same pairs, two different pictures.
extending.stemEs: La tabla de boletos y la gráfica de boletos son dos representaciones. ¿Cuál enunciado sobre ellas es verdadero?
extending.explanationEs: Cada fila de la tabla se ubica como un punto, así que ambos muestran costo = 45 × boletos — la tabla de forma numérica, la gráfica de forma visual.
hintsEs: ¿De dónde vienen los puntos de la gráfica?
Cada fila de la tabla se convierte en un punto.
Los mismos pares, dos dibujos distintos.
choicesEs: Ambos muestran la misma relación — la tabla con valores numéricos, la gráfica de forma más visual
La gráfica muestra una relación distinta a la de la tabla
Solo la tabla puede mostrar que el costo aumenta con los boletos
Solo la gráfica es una representación matemática real

extending.stem: Nakai earns $26.25 in simple interest every year. On the graph of years vs. interest earned, which point represents 4 years?
extending.explanation: After 4 years the interest earned is 4 × 26.25 = 105 dollars, so the point is (4, 105).
choiceFeedback: $26.25 is the interest for 1 year, not 4.
$78.75 is the interest after 3 years — one year short.
$750 is the principal Nakai deposited, not interest earned.
hints: How much interest arrives EACH year?
Four years means four equal payments of $26.25.
Multiply 26.25 by 4.
extending.stemEs: Nakai gana $26.25 de interés simple cada año. En la gráfica de años vs. interés ganado, ¿cuál punto representa 4 años?
extending.explanationEs: Después de 4 años el interés ganado es 4 × 26.25 = 105 dólares, así que el punto es (4, 105).
hintsEs: ¿Cuánto interés llega CADA año?
Cuatro años significan cuatro pagos iguales de $26.25.
Multiplica 26.25 por 4.

extending.stem: After 10 minutes, the Sandia Peak tram has traveled 12,000 feet. The whole ascent is 18,000 feet. How much farther must it travel to reach the top?
extending.explanation: The remaining distance is 18,000 − 12,000 = 6,000 feet — which matches the last 5 minutes at 1,200 feet per minute.
choiceFeedback: 12,000 feet is the distance already traveled, not what remains.
Check with the rate: 5 remaining minutes × 1,200 feet is 6,000, not 5,000.
1,200 feet is only one more minute of travel — 5 minutes remain.
hints: How is 'distance remaining' related to the total?
Subtract the distance traveled from 18,000.
Check your answer: 5 minutes remain at 1,200 feet per minute.
extending.stemEs: Después de 10 minutos, el tranvía de Sandia Peak ha recorrido 12,000 pies. Todo el ascenso son 18,000 pies. ¿Cuánto más debe recorrer para llegar a la cima?
extending.explanationEs: La distancia que falta es 18,000 − 12,000 = 6,000 pies — que coincide con los últimos 5 minutos a 1,200 pies por minuto.
hintsEs: ¿Cómo se relaciona la 'distancia que falta' con el total?
Resta la distancia recorrida de 18,000.
Revisa tu respuesta: quedan 5 minutos a 1,200 pies por minuto.
choicesEs: 6,000 pies
12,000 pies
5,000 pies
1,200 pies

extending.stem: A second tram travels 900 feet per minute. If both trams are graphed on the same axes (minutes vs. feet), how do the graphs compare?
choices: The Sandia Peak line (1,200 ft/min) rises more steeply than the 900 ft/min line
The 900 ft/min line rises more steeply
extending.explanation: Compare what each tram does in one minute. The Sandia tram climbs 1,200 feet. The other climbs only 900. A faster rate makes a steeper line.
choiceFeedback: Steepness follows the rate: 900 feet per minute rises LESS each minute than 1,200.
Different rates give different points — at 1 minute one graph is at 900 and the other at 1,200.
Both trams gain distance over time, so both lines rise.
hints: Compare where each graph is after 1 minute.
One is at 900 feet, the other at 1,200 feet.
The faster rate climbs more per minute — steeper.
extending.stemEs: Un segundo tranvía viaja 900 pies por minuto. Si ambos tranvías se grafican en los mismos ejes (minutos vs. pies), ¿cómo se comparan las gráficas?
extending.explanationEs: Compara lo que hace cada tranvía en un minuto. El tranvía de Sandia sube 1,200 pies. El otro sube solo 900. Una tasa más rápida hace una línea más empinada.
hintsEs: Compara dónde está cada gráfica después de 1 minuto.
Uno está en 900 pies, el otro en 1,200 pies.
La tasa más rápida sube más por minuto — más empinada.
choicesEs: La línea de Sandia Peak (1,200 pies/min) sube más empinada que la línea de 900 pies/min
La línea de 900 pies/min sube más empinada
Las dos líneas son idénticas
La línea de 900 pies/min va hacia abajo

extending.stem: The ticket graph has “Number of tickets” across the bottom and “Total cost ($)” up the side. Rowan plots the first ticket as the point (45, 1). What did Rowan misunderstand — and what does his point actually claim about tickets and money?
extending.stemEs: La gráfica de boletos tiene “Número de boletos” en la parte de abajo y “Costo total ($)” en el lado. Rowan grafica el primer boleto como el punto (45, 1). ¿Qué entendió mal Rowan y qué afirma en realidad su punto sobre los boletos y el dinero?
extending.modelAnswer: Rowan swapped the order. The independent variable goes first, so one ticket at $45 is the point (1, 45). His point (45, 1) says that 45 tickets cost one dollar altogether, which is not what the table shows.
extending.modelAnswerEs: Rowan invirtió el orden. La variable independiente va primero, así que un boleto de $45 es el punto (1, 45). Su punto (45, 1) dice que 45 boletos cuestan un dólar en total, que no es lo que muestra la tabla.

extending.stem: Two trams both start at the bottom at 0 minutes. One climbs 1,200 feet each minute, the other 900. Both are graphed on the same axes with minutes across. Without working out a single point, how can you tell which line belongs to the faster tram?
extending.stemEs: Dos tranvías arrancan abajo a los 0 minutos. Uno sube 1,200 pies por minuto y el otro 900. Ambos se grafican en los mismos ejes con los minutos en el eje horizontal. Sin calcular ni un punto, ¿cómo sabes cuál recta es la del tranvía más rápido?
choices: Its line rises more steeply — it gains more feet in the same minute
Its line starts higher up the vertical axis
Its line is longer than the other one
You cannot tell without plotting points for both
choicesEs: Su recta sube más empinada: gana más pies en el mismo minuto
Su recta empieza más arriba en el eje vertical
Su recta es más larga que la otra
No se puede saber sin graficar puntos de las dos
extending.explanation: Both trams start at 0 feet at 0 minutes, so both lines begin at the same corner. The only thing that can differ is how fast they climb, and that is the steepness: 1,200 feet in one minute against 900.
extending.explanationEs: Los dos tranvías empiezan en 0 pies a los 0 minutos, así que las dos rectas parten de la misma esquina. Lo único que puede diferir es qué tan rápido suben, y eso es lo empinado: 1,200 pies en un minuto frente a 900.
choiceFeedback: Both start at 0 feet at 0 minutes. Where do the two lines begin?
Length depends on how far the graph is drawn, not on the tram's speed.
Compare one minute on each line. Which one has climbed further by then?
choiceFeedbackEs: Los dos empiezan en 0 pies a los 0 minutos. ¿Dónde comienzan las dos rectas?
El largo depende de hasta dónde se dibuje la gráfica, no de la velocidad del tranvía.
Compara un minuto en cada recta. ¿Cuál ha subido más para entonces?
hints: At 0 minutes, how high is each tram?
Look at what has happened to each line after exactly one minute.
hintsEs: A los 0 minutos, ¿a qué altura está cada tranvía?
Mira qué le pasó a cada recta después de exactamente un minuto.

extending.stem: Claim: “If two quantities grow together, the points on their graph always lie on a straight line.” Always, sometimes, or never true?
extending.stemEs: Afirmación: “Si dos cantidades crecen juntas, los puntos de su gráfica siempre quedan en línea recta”. ¿Siempre, a veces o nunca es verdadera?
choices: Sometimes — only when the quantity grows by the same amount each step
Always — growing together is what makes a line
Never — real data never lines up
Sometimes — only when both quantities are measured in the same unit
choicesEs: A veces — solo cuando la cantidad crece la misma cantidad en cada paso
Siempre — crecer juntas es lo que forma una recta
Nunca — los datos reales nunca se alinean
A veces — solo cuando ambas cantidades se miden en la misma unidad
extending.explanation: The tickets rise by the same $45 every time, so they line up. The side and area of a square both grow — (1, 1), (2, 4), (3, 9) — but the jumps are 3 then 5, so those points bend upward instead of forming a line.
extending.explanationEs: Los boletos suben los mismos $45 cada vez, así que se alinean. El lado y el área de un cuadrado crecen los dos — (1, 1), (2, 4), (3, 9) — pero los saltos son 3 y luego 5, así que esos puntos se curvan hacia arriba en vez de formar una recta.
choiceFeedback: Try side and area of a square: (1, 1), (2, 4), (3, 9). Are the jumps equal?
The ticket graph does line up. Check the jumps between its points.
Tickets and dollars are different units and they still form a line.
choiceFeedbackEs: Prueba el lado y el área de un cuadrado: (1, 1), (2, 4), (3, 9). ¿Son iguales los saltos?
La gráfica de boletos sí se alinea. Revisa los saltos entre sus puntos.
Boletos y dólares son unidades distintas y aun así forman una recta.
hints: Find one growing relationship whose points do NOT line up.
List (1, 1), (2, 4), (3, 9) and look at the size of each jump.
hintsEs: Encuentra una relación creciente cuyos puntos NO se alineen.
Escribe (1, 1), (2, 4), (3, 9) y mira el tamaño de cada salto.

extending.stem: A different event's ticket graph passes through the point (4, 100). What does one ticket cost, and where would the point for 7 tickets sit?
extending.stemEs: La gráfica de boletos de otro evento pasa por el punto (4, 100). ¿Cuánto cuesta un boleto y dónde quedaría el punto para 7 boletos?
choices: $25 each, and the point would be (7, 175)
$25 each, and the point would be (175, 7)
$400 each, and the point would be (7, 2800)
There is not enough information to find the cost of one ticket
choicesEs: $25 cada uno, y el punto quedaría en (7, 175)
$25 cada uno, y el punto quedaría en (175, 7)
$400 cada uno, y el punto quedaría en (7, 2800)
No hay información suficiente para hallar el costo de un boleto
extending.explanation: The point (4, 100) says 4 tickets cost $100 altogether, so one ticket is 100 ÷ 4 = $25. Seven tickets are 7 × 25 = $175, plotted as (7, 175) with the number of tickets first.
extending.explanationEs: El punto (4, 100) dice que 4 boletos cuestan $100 en total, así que un boleto cuesta 100 ÷ 4 = $25. Siete boletos son 7 × 25 = $175, graficado como (7, 175) con el número de boletos primero.
choiceFeedback: The cost is right, but check the order — which quantity goes first?
That multiplies instead of dividing. 4 tickets cost $100 in total, not $100 each.
One point is enough here: it gives you 4 tickets and their total cost.
choiceFeedbackEs: El costo está bien, pero revisa el orden: ¿qué cantidad va primero?
Eso multiplica en vez de dividir. 4 boletos cuestan $100 en total, no $100 cada uno.
Un punto basta aquí: te da 4 boletos y su costo total.
hints: What do the two numbers in (4, 100) stand for?
Split the $100 between the 4 tickets first.
hintsEs: ¿Qué representan los dos números de (4, 100)?
Primero reparte los $100 entre los 4 boletos.

extending.stem: Every graph in this lesson rises to the right. Invent a situation where the dependent quantity goes DOWN as the independent quantity goes up. Give three ordered pairs, say what each quantity is, and describe what your graph looks like.
extending.stemEs: Todas las gráficas de esta lección suben hacia la derecha. Inventa una situación donde la cantidad dependiente BAJE mientras la independiente sube. Da tres pares ordenados, di qué es cada cantidad y describe cómo se ve tu gráfica.
extending.modelAnswer: Minutes riding the tram and miles still left to travel. At 0 minutes there are 12 miles left, at 1 minute 10 miles, at 2 minutes 8 miles: (0, 12), (1, 10), (2, 8). Two miles disappear every minute, so the points drop by the same amount each step and the line falls to the right.
extending.modelAnswerEs: Minutos viajando en el tranvía y millas que faltan por recorrer. A los 0 minutos faltan 12 millas, a 1 minuto 10 millas, a 2 minutos 8 millas: (0, 12), (1, 10), (2, 8). Desaparecen dos millas cada minuto, así que los puntos bajan lo mismo en cada paso y la recta cae hacia la derecha.

extending.stem: On the tram graph — minutes across, feet climbed up the side — a classmate marks the point (0, 0) and says it is meaningless. Do you agree? Say what (0, 0) claims about the tram, and why the line passes through it.
extending.stemEs: En la gráfica del tranvía — minutos en el eje horizontal, pies subidos en el vertical — un compañero marca el punto (0, 0) y dice que no significa nada. ¿Estás de acuerdo? Di qué afirma (0, 0) sobre el tranvía y por qué la recta pasa por ahí.
extending.modelAnswer: I disagree. The point (0, 0) says that after 0 minutes the tram has climbed 0 feet, which is exactly where it starts. It is the most reliable point on the graph, and the line passes through it because the tram begins the climb from the bottom.
extending.modelAnswerEs: No estoy de acuerdo. El punto (0, 0) dice que después de 0 minutos el tranvía ha subido 0 pies, que es justo donde empieza. Es el punto más confiable de la gráfica, y la recta pasa por ahí porque el tranvía comienza la subida desde abajo.
sentenceStems: The line passes through it because ___ .

extending.title: Fix our table's thinking

workedExample.label: The problem
workedExample.work: Why is the line on the football ticket graph dashed instead of solid?
workedExample.workEs: ¿Por qué la línea de la gráfica de boletos de fútbol americano es punteada en vez de continua?

workedExample.label: A classmate at our table answered
workedExample.labelEs: Un compañero de nuestra mesa respondió

extending.correctWork: The correct answer is You can only buy whole numbers of tickets, so the points between whole numbers do not make sense. You cannot buy 2.5 tickets, so only the whole-number points represent real purchases — the dashes show the trend without claiming the in-between points are possible.
extending.correctWorkEs: La respuesta correcta es Solo se pueden comprar números enteros de boletos, así que los puntos entre números enteros no tienen sentido. No puedes comprar 2.5 boletos, así que solo los puntos con números enteros representan compras reales — las líneas punteadas muestran la tendencia sin afirmar que los puntos intermedios sean posibles.
hints: Could you buy half a ticket?
hintsEs: ¿Podrías comprar medio boleto?

practice.commonMistake: Reversing the coordinates of a point — writing (cost, tickets) instead of (tickets, cost). The independent variable always comes first in the ordered pair.

questions.stem: Songs cost $2 each. Which is the independent variable?
questions.explanation: The number of songs is what you choose. The total cost depends on that choice, so cost is the dependent variable.

questions.stem: "The longer you run, the more calories you burn." Which is the dependent variable?
questions.explanation: Calories burned depends on how long you run, so calories is the dependent variable.

questions.stem: A plant grows taller each day. Which sentence is correct?
choices: Height depends on the number of days
The number of days depends on height
Neither one depends on the other
questions.explanation: Days pass on their own; the height responds to them. So height is dependent and days is independent.

questions.stem: In any relationship between two quantities, the independent variable is the one that…
questions.explanation: The independent variable is the input you get to choose. The dependent variable responds to it.
